PalletPoseStamped gains the chosen candidate's source index as the pallet sent through stage 2, and the source indices of the other class-matched candidates in that same Detection2DArray as deferred. Those indices are the slots extract_detection_candidates already stored. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the roster is this capture while the scene can still change. findings: Stage 2 is the latency that multiplies with each detection sent. Liu, Tuzel, Veeraraghavan, and Chellappa (CVPR 2010) measured classic chamfer at 17.59 us per hypothesis and oriented chamfer at 51.50 us, mean over templates of 1,610 points; directional chamfer was 0.40 us. Classic chamfer grows linearly with template points. Their directional matcher evaluated 1.05 million hypotheses in 0.42 s, and one object 3D pose took 0.71 s that way against 29.1 s for classic chamfer and 65.3 s for oriented chamfer. estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 scores the default pocket prototype once: contour spacing 0.03 m is 182 points (outer 94, two pockets 44 each). The free search is 21 x 31 x 31 = 20,181 plus 13 x 25 x 25 = 8,125, 28,306 hypotheses. The prior grids run when the free cost is above about 0.00623 m, because prior_lambda 3.0 times (1 - confidence) then exceeds lambda_floor 0.05, and they add 21 x 21 x 21 = 9,261 plus another 8,125, 45,692 hypotheses in all. Scaling their 17.59 us by 182/1,610 is about 1.99 us per hypothesis, a serial envelope of about 56 ms for the free grids and about 91 ms if the prior grids also run. That envelope is not a clock of this node: the loop is OpenMP, and it evaluates every cell rather than their early-out directional matcher. A deferred source index does not enter the search.

Posing every class-matched detection with a learned refiner has the same per-object multiplier, which select_detection already avoids by sending stage 2 once. Labbe, Carpentier, Aubry, and Sivic (CosyPose, ECCV 2020) measured 190 ms to pose all candidates for 4 views and 6 detections per view, one coarse iteration and one refinement iteration, inside a 320 ms scene (association 40 ms, scene refinement 90 ms). Wen, Yang, Kautz, and Birchfield (FoundationPose) measured 1.3 s per object on an i9-10980XE and RTX 3090 (initialization 4 ms, refinement 0.88 s, selection 0.42 s); tracking is about 32 Hz and is still one object. The distance image inside each chamfer call is the small fixed part of that bill. OpenCV pull 28636, Jetson Orin geometric mean, 640x480 DIST_L2 DIST_MASK_PRECISE on CV_8U is 0.788 ms on 4.x and 0.737 ms with the patch. This node calls cv::distanceTransform with DIST_L2 and DIST_MASK_PRECISE on an 8-bit edge mask once per posed detection, on the padded face raster rather than a 640x480 frame, so 0.788 ms is that call at the published size. Deferred candidates skip both the grid and that image.

Both lists on PalletPoseStamped are one int32 and a short int32[] on the pose the handling process already reads, and that payload sits where ROS 2 latency does not move. Kronauer, Pohlmann, Matthe, Smejkal, and Fettweis (ROS 2 Foxy, desktop i7-8700, localhost UDP) measured equal latency at 128 B, 1 KB, and 10 KB; it rose at 100 KB and 500 KB, past the 64 KB UDP fragment. Fast DDS CDR (rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps pull 150, mean of three runs, pinned core) serializes a String in 10.7 ns, a Header in 14.3 ns, a Vector3 in 9.5 ns, and a Pose in 14.9 ns; a nested Marker mean is 394 ns. The message already carries this pair RGB and depth stamps, so the roster is source indices, the slots extract_detection_candidates stored, not another stamp per candidate. Leaving the lists only on a diagnostic the success path does not use forces a second delivery. Yu ROS2-pubsub-benchmark, same-process ROS 2 C++ P90 per hop on an i7-9700K, is 113 us at 100 Hz and 138 us at 1 kHz for a small message. That hop is far below one extra chamfer search, and the rich pose does not pay it when both lists ride the message the controller already takes.

The slow message shape is an array of non-primitives, which this roster is not. Cyclone DDS issue 346 (ROS 2 Galactic, Ryzen 7 4800H, no subscriber): a TestElement[] of 5,000 elements, each holding a builtin_interfaces/Time, requested at 1,000 Hz and measured about 369 Hz, with ros2 topic hz about 30 Hz. Fast DDS at 5,000 of those elements also showed about 30 Hz on topic hz. The time was field-by-field serialization. The same issue notes that high-rate messages are usually a header plus an array of primitives, and that replacing the array-of-structs with a struct-of-arrays is the fast shape; a trivial 80 KB message on loopback was about 35,000 msg/s in ddsperf. One int32 for the pallet sent through stage 2 and one int32[] of the other source indices are that primitive side. On estimate failure the same two lists go on the diagnostic, the only result that path publishes, and they stay under the 10 KB plateau. The two early returns publish nothing, so they add no DDS hop.
